title: Replica theory for the rate functional of the empirical spectral distribution function of diluted Hermitian matrices
abstract: We develop a replica-based framework for the scaled cumulant-generating functional of the empirical spectral distribution function $i_C$ of diluted Hermitian random matrices. Within a replica-symmetric saddle-point assumption, this construction yields a candidate rate functional for fluctuations of $i_C$. As an illustrative application, we consider adjacency matrices of unweighted Erdős-Rényi random graphs with mean degree $c$. We derive explicit expressions for the first two cumulants of $i_C$, indicate how higher cumulants can be obtained from further functional derivatives, and compute the rate function of Fourier coefficients, equivalently of selected linear spectral statistics. The replica-symmetric predictions are tested against exact numerical diagonalization and show good agreement in the accessible fluctuation regime. The approach provides a basis for studying rate functionals of spectral observables in sparse random matrix ensembles.
summary: This work applies advanced techniques from spin-glass theory (replica method) to calculate the rate functional governing fluctuations of the spectral distribution in sparse random matrices. By deriving explicit formulas for cumulants and comparing them against numerical data, the authors establish a powerful theoretical framework for analyzing spectral observables in complex disordered systems.
main_problem: The paper develops a replica-based framework to determine the rate functional for fluctuations of the empirical spectral distribution function ($i_C$) in diluted Hermitian random matrices.
main_result: It derives explicit expressions for the first two cumulants and computes candidate rate functions ($\Psi[\zeta]$) for linear spectral statistics, showing good agreement with numerical diagonalization in the accessible fluctuation regime.
method: The core method involves using replica theory from spin-glass physics to calculate the scaled cumulant-generating functional ($F[\mu]$) via a replica-symmetric saddle-point approximation.
model_or_system: The system under study is diluted Hermitian random matrices, exemplified by the adjacency matrices of unweighted Erdős–Rényi random graphs with a mean degree $c$. The analysis focuses on spectral statistics derived from these matrices.
key_observables: Empirical spectral distribution function ($i_C(x)$), cumulants ($\kappa_1, \kappa_2$), and the rate functional $\Psi[\zeta]$ for linear spectral statistics (e.g., Fourier coefficients).
important_parameters: Mean degree $c$, system size $N$ (analyzed in the thermodynamic limit $N 	o \infty$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the replica-symmetric saddle-point ansatz and assumes that a large-deviation principle holds for $i_C$.
figures_summary: Figures compare theoretical predictions for $\kappa_1$, $N\kappa_2$, and the rate function $\psi$ against results from exact numerical diagonalization, demonstrating quantitative agreement.
paper_structure: The paper builds up the formalism by first defining the generating functional using replicas, then deriving explicit formulas for cumulants via functional derivatives, and finally computing the rate function $\psi(u)$ through transformations relating it to the cumulant-generating functional $f( eta)$.
why_interesting: While focused on random matrices, the use of replica theory and large deviation principles is a powerful mathematical tool applicable to complex systems where mean-field approximations are necessary, providing rigorous statistical descriptions.
